question: does screenshot injection hold at web-medium scale (240 questions, union-store superset)?
design: full-population paired A/B: text arm vs anchored-screenshot injection arm (mean 5.65 images/question), both arms on glm-5.3-flash (vision) with glm-5.3 judge, plain hybrid retrieval shared. Union-store superset haystack (each question's official 387-500-trajectory subset is contained in the seeded union - accuracy is a LOWER BOUND for the protocol). Two-stage fixed answerer (thinking-budget + fallback) from the start; empty-answer audit applies.
findings: Screenshot injection MORE than holds at medium scale: +23.75pp (web-small was +19.2pp) - against a 5x deeper, union-superset haystack.
dynamic-environment-abs 0.0 -> 0.381: the abstention variants of the hardest stratum flip from zero to answerable when the answer page's screenshot reaches the answerer.
static-environment 0.550 and procedure 0.548: both cross the 50pp line - the mm operating point sits 2.2pp below the medium-tier LAFS floor (RAG 45.9@0.3s) overall (43.75 vs 45.9).
Latency stays in the fast band (p50 3.3s) - the frontier gap to the LAFS scoring line is now a 2.2pp accuracy gap, not latency.
honest_reading: union-store lower bound (superset haystack); glm-5.3-flash answerer + glm-5.3 judge (same-family disclosure as all V2 points); plain non-orchestrated retrieval shared by both arms so the A/B delta attributes to screenshots alone; residual = questions whose answer page never ranks into top-12 (the retrieval-side class), plus procedure-abs 0.15 where procedural text, not vision, is the bottleneck.
